catalog_quote: Besides the loss of vowel harmony, Krymchak treats the common Turkic rule of ultimate stress rather inconsistently. Cases are observed, as ˈdoğru 'straight,' tengrØ < *tengri 'deity,' or ˈvaxit 'time' where the stress shifts away from the ultimate syllable. ... These seemingly unrelated phenomena can be explained in terms of a single vocalic hierarchy: (3) a. [i] > [e] > [a] > [o] > [u] > [ï] which can be rewritten in a more traditional form as: (3) b. front high V > front low V > back V. The hierarchy predicts that the vowels to the left in (3a) will retain their properties (i.e., they will withstand reduction and harmonic assimilation). It also predicts that they will attract stress and control the vocalic properties of the environment (harmony) more efficiently than the vowels to the right in (3a), irrespective of their position in the word. new_statements.quote: В большинстве слов ударение стоит на последнем слоге. Когда слово переходит в другой падеж, ударение также остаётся в конце слова. Например: адаˈ «остров», адалардаˈн «с островов».
new_statements.translation: In most words the stress is on the last syllable. When a word takes another case form, the stress likewise stays at the end of the word. E.g. adá 'island', adalardán 'from the islands'.
new_statements.citation: Russian Wikipedia, «Крымчакский язык», раздел «Фонетика» (no inline reference; section literature: Реби Д. И. 2004, Крымчакский язык. Крымчакско-русский словарь, Симферополь; Ачкинази Ш. Е., Миреев В. А., Казаченко Б. Н. 2019, Крымчакская лексикография, грамматика и фразеология, Симферополь: Ариал). Tertiary; the two accessible primary descriptions (Rebi et al. 1997; Güllüdağ 2005) are silent on stress.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: the saved page contains, at <li id="mw6w"> (last bullet of h3 'Фонетика и фонология'), exactly: «В большинстве слов ударение стоит на последнем слоге. Когда слово переходит в другой падеж, ударение также остаётся в конце слова. Например: адаˈ «остров», адалардаˈн «с островов».» — verbatim as reported (the derived, line 214, shows the same sentence with stray spaces from tag stripping). No inline <sup> reference is attached to that bullet; the article's Литература lists Реби 2004 and Ачкинази, Миреев & Казаченко 2019, as the other reader says. Reading of that sentence = fixed: final syllable (stress word-final, stays final under suffixation, hedged 'в большинстве слов'); I agree…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress on the final syllable of the word, moving onto inflectional (case/plural) suffixes so that it remains word-final; 'most words' implies unlisted exceptions (as in Crimean Tatar: certain clitic-like suffixes, adverbs, loans).
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'в большинстве слов' (in most words); no exceptions listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation/inflected forms (ада → адалардан). Unsourced tertiary statement; consistent with the Middle-dialect Crimean Tatar system that Rebi et al. 1997 say Krymchak morphology coincides with, but no primary Krymchak description opened here states it.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources treat Krymchak (кърымчах тыльы, 'чагатай' self-name until late 19th c.) as the Jewish (Rabbanite) ethnolect of Middle-dialect Crimean Tatar (Karasubazar/Simferopol); Rebi et al. 1997 state its morphology 'coincides with the middle dialect of Crimean Tatar' (crim1257). Güllüdağ 2005 is based on 1928-1930 Latin-script school texts and Rebi's materials, not on speech. Any stress statement found later should be checked against Crimean Tatar final-stress descriptions for independence.
